edges.relation: Both use hierarchical spatial decomposition; FMM extends Barnes-Hut with translation operators to achieve O(N) vs O(N log N)
Barnes-Hut tree walk is a handcrafted multi-scale message-passing scheme; GNNs learn the message functions from data
Tree traversal is inherently serial and GPU-hostile; recent work (RT-BarnesHut) reformulates it for ray-tracing cores
Algebraically equivalent: leapfrog and Verlet are the same method with different variable orderings
Symplecticity guarantees bounded energy error, which the monitor detects as oscillation rather than drift
Naive adaptive stepping breaks symplecticity; preserving it requires time-transformation techniques (as in SQQ-PTQ)
Boids cohesion rule is a linear attraction; replacing it with 1/r^2 attraction produces gravity-like emergent dynamics
Both define local neighborhoods and compute interactions from neighbor information; GNNs learn the interaction rules that boids prescribe
GNNs learn dynamics from trajectory data; PINNs embed the governing PDE directly into the loss — complementary approaches to neural physics
GNN learns full interaction from scratch; hybrid uses classical multipole as a backbone and learns only the residual correction
FMM provides the classical force approximation that the neural hybrid corrects; the hybrid reduces FMM order requirements
Both combine physics knowledge with neural networks; PINN embeds the PDE, hybrid embeds the algorithmic approximation
Verlet's simple update rule maps perfectly to GPU parallelism: each thread updates one particle with no data dependencies between particles
Energy drift measurements can drive adaptive timestep selection: increase dt when drift is small, decrease when large
If gravity emerges from local rules, a PINN could discover those local rules from observed gravitational dynamics
GNN inference on particle graphs maps to GPU scatter-gather operations; both exploit parallelism over particles
Verlet's symplecticity means the energy monitor should detect bounded oscillation, providing a validation check

bridge_chains.name: classical_to_learned_physics
bridge_chains.description: Progression from handcrafted hierarchical approximation through hybrid classical-neural methods to fully learned particle dynamics. Each step trades explicit physics knowledge for learned flexibility.

bridge_chains.name: biology_to_astrophysics
bridge_chains.description: Bridge from behavioral ecology (boids) through emergent gravity from local rules, neural discovery of governing equations, to symplectic integration of those equations. Shows how gravity simulation connects to collective animal behavior.

bridge_chains.name: hardware_aware_simulation
bridge_chains.description: From GPU hardware exploitation through minimal-memory integration to runtime quality monitoring and adaptive control. The full stack of building a performant, validated gravity sim.

bridge_chains.name: accuracy_hierarchy
bridge_chains.description: Chain of increasing sophistication in accuracy control: from monitoring energy drift, through symplectic guarantees, adaptive timestepping, O(N) force evaluation, to neural residual correction.

bridge_chains.name: emergence_to_formalism
bridge_chains.description: From bottom-up emergence (local swarm rules producing gravity-like behavior) to top-down formalism (PINNs embedding Poisson's equation). Crosses from artificial life through ML to mathematical physics.
